report.summary: Host WS-HR-08 shows active command-and-control beaconing from an unauthorized process running a system binary name out of a user-writable directory.

claims.text: The alerting tool EDR reported that svchost.exe was running from an unusual folder on host WS-HR-08.
An instance of svchost.exe (PID 6600) was executed from C:\Users\Public by explorer.exe (PID 2000) under user CORP\rpatel with command line 'svchost.exe -k netsvcs'.
The suspicious process established 14 external network connections to IP 203.0.113.99 on uncommon port 8443.
Beaconing analysis revealed machine-like regular connection intervals averaging approximately 120 seconds with a low coefficient of variation, indicating command-and-control activity.

techniques.name: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location

recommended_next_steps: Isolate host WS-HR-08 from the network to prevent further command-and-control communication.
Terminate the malicious process running from C:\Users\Public (PID 6600).
Collect memory and disk artifacts from WS-HR-08 for forensic analysis.
Perform network hunts across the enterprise for outbound connections to IP 203.0.113.99 on port 8443.
Review execution logs for other hosts executing binaries from C:\Users\Public or other user-writable folders.
